basis: Fatty-acid oxidation disorder with defining infantile hepatic and cardiac disease; myopathy occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic injury is occasional.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic dysfunction characterizes the severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular form despite occasional frequency tags on individual hepatic phenotypes.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy and serious arrhythmias characterize the severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular phenotype.

basis: Defining skeletal dysostosis, arthrogryposis, pulmonary hypoplasia and persistent cutaneous webbing across joints.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: multiple cutaneous pterygia are explicitly defining structural skin malformations that restrict joints.

basis: Malformation of venous channels within the spleen; no established impairment of blood cells or splenic hematologic function.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenic location of malformed vessels alone does not establish disease of the spleen as a blood organ.

basis: Defining oral and digital malformations; intellectual disability 8/8 and hearing impairment 2/3. Cardiac and ocular defects reported in 1/3 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 8/8 and developmental delay in 5/5 support common intrinsic neurodevelopmental impairment beyond the defining oral-digital malformations.

basis: Spirometra larval infection; destructive subcutaneous invasion with inflammatory nodules occurs in roughly 30-50%. CNS and ocular frequencies vary geographically.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous larval invasion causes inflammatory nodules in roughly 30-50%; this common site does not define every form of sparganosis.

basis: Defining otomandibular dysplasia; ocular colobomas/visual impairment and dental agenesis/malocclusion each occur in 30-79%. Speech delay alone does not establish CNS injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: structural colobomas and visual impairment occur in 30-79%, accompanying the defining otomandibular dysplasia; palpebral slant alone would not suffice.

basis: Immune-mediated skin and mucosal epithelial necrosis; destructive oral mucositis is defining and occurs in about 90%. Supplied damaging ocular phenotypes occur in 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destructive oral mucositis is a defining mucosal manifestation, present in about 90%; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Defining porencephaly and cerebellar malformations; associated cardiac defects and corneal clouding have no established frequency supporting the 30% threshold.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations are reported associated findings, without an established frequency of at least 30% or evidence that they are major diagnostic criteria.

basis: Severe peroxisomal disorder with defining cerebral and hepatic disease; hearing impairment 4/4. Ocular disease omitted at cap; renal cysts alone do not establish dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic dysfunction is a defining component of severe Zellweger disease, supported by transaminase elevation in 2/2 and hepatomegaly/jaundice.
decisions.neurologic: primary: cerebral malformations and profound neurodevelopmental impairment define severe Zellweger disease; developmental delay is reported in 4/4.

basis: Hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal vasopressin deficiency defines endocrine dysfunction; polyuria does not establish renal damage, and broader neurologic injury is not intrinsic.

decisions.neurologic: none: isolated hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal hormone deficiency is captured by the endocrine axis; additional brain injury depends on the underlying cause.
